chunks: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Dawud al-Raqqi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, moderation is a matter that Allah loves, and indeed, extravagance is a matter that Allah hates, even if it is the throwing away of date stones, for they are suitable for something, and even if it is pouring out your leftover drink.

key_terms.النَّوَاهَ: Date stones (pits), used here as an example of small waste
key_terms.الْقَصْدُ: Moderation or balance in conduct and consumption

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about wasting small amounts of food or water?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that divine love for moderation (al-qasd) and hatred for extravagance (al-saraf) extend to micro-wastes, using date stones and leftover water as tangible examples of neglected utility. This reflects the Shia ethical principle that resource conservation is an act of worship, preventing the subtle accumulation of waste that leads to broader economic and spiritual depletion.
